CIRCUIT: a randomly-generated MOSFET network. Top rail (y~300) carries the 5V V-DC(#0) whose other side goes to GND(#1). Three horizontal rails below it (y~438, y~538, y~590) plus a bottom return rail (y~723). 14 components, 10 nets.

NET MAP (names as emitted by finalize.py):
  0   = V-DC(#0) right terminal + GND(#1). The only grounded node.
  n1  = top rail y~300: 0.0 (V-DC left), 2.0 (drain of MOSFET-N #2), 3.0 (drain of MOSFET-P #3), 4.1 (top/cathode lead of the 3V zener #4 via the x~62 column).
  n2  = the gate wire of MOSFET-N #2: from its gate bar at x~352 left along y~378 to x~293, then straight down (crossing the y=438 and y=538 rails at S9 and S13) to y~592, then left to the top terminal of V-AC #11 (5V/3kHz). Terminals 2.1 and 11.0.
  n3  = rail y~438 unioned with the x~386 column: 2.2 (source of #2), 3.2 (source of #3), 5.0 (drain of MOSFET-P #5), 6.0 (drain of MOSFET-N #6).
  n4  = rail y~538 plus the x~62 column below the zener: 3.1 (gate of #3, via the x~166 drop), 4.0 (bottom/anode of the zener), 6.1 (gate of #6), 9.0 (top terminal of V-AC #9, 1V/2kHz).
  n5  = gate of MOSFET-P #5 (lead exits right at y~488, runs to x~890 then down) + 8.0 (top of I-AC #8, 1A/2kHz).
  n6  = rail y~590 right half: 5.1 (source of #5, dropping from y~503 to y~588), 7.1 (right end of the 1k resistor), 12.0 (drain of MOSFET-P #12).
  n7  = rail y~590 left half: 6.2 (source of #6), 7.0 (left end of the 1k resistor), 13.0 (drain of MOSFET-N #13).
  n8  = bottom return rail y~723: 8.1, 9.1, 10.1, 11.1, 12.2 (source of #12), 13.1 (source of #13) and 13.2 (gate of #13 - its gate lead goes left at y~677 then down to the rail at x~310, site S39). #13 therefore has gate and source on the same node; that is what the drawing shows.
  n9  = gate of MOSFET-P #12 (lead exits right at y~687, steps up to y~595 then right to x~806) + 10.0 (top of I-AC #10, 5A/3kHz).

JUDGEMENT CALLS (intersections):
  S9 (296,438) deg=5 - CROSSING (agrees with tracer default, recorded explicitly). zoom at 12x shows a textbook sideways S-jog: the x~293 column bulges right to x~298 just above the rail, crosses at y=438, then swings back left to x~291 below it. That is this drafter's 'not connected' mark. Junction here would have shorted MOSFET #2's gate onto the y=438 rail (drains/sources of #3/#5/#2/#6) and left V-AC #11's top terminal on a 1-terminal net.
  S13 (282,538) deg=4 - OVERRIDDEN from the tracer's 'junction' to CROSSING. zoom at 12x shows the same S-jog signature as S9: the column arrives at x~282, deviates right to x~287 while passing the rail at y=540, then curves back left and leaves at x~275 heading down to y~592. Two small left-hand pen ticks at y~535 and y~558 are lead-in/lead-out artefacts, not branches. Decisive corroboration: with S13 read as a crossing, the column below it runs to y~592, turns left and lands exactly on the top terminal of V-AC #11 - which the tracer had stranded as the 1-terminal net 'n11'. Reading it as a junction would (a) leave V-AC #11's top terminal on a dead 1-terminal net and (b) tie MOSFET #2's gate to the zener/gate rail, contradicting the drawn jog.
  S10 (386,438) deg=4 - JUNCTION (agrees with default, recorded explicitly). inkmap at (386,438) shows a plain X: the x=386 column is a uniform 3px stroke straight through y=414..462 and the rail is a uniform 2px stroke straight through; no solder dot (no blob wider than the strokes in both axes) and no jog. Since this drafter demonstrably draws a jog when he means 'not connected' (S9, S13 on the very same two wires), a bare crossing here reads as a real junction. The crossing reading would have split this node into {#3 source, #5 drain} and {#2 source, #6 drain} - electrically sane but against the ink prior and against the drafter's own habit on this sheet.
  S1 (225,305), S2 (387,306) - clean T's where the #3 and #2 drain columns meet the top rail. JUNCTION.
  S12 (158,536) - T, the x~166 drop from MOSFET #3's gate terminating on the y=538 rail. JUNCTION.
  S14 (68,538) - T, the y=538 rail terminating on the through-going x~62 column (zener bottom above, V-AC #9 top below). JUNCTION.
  S17 (698,588) - T, the y=590 rail's right half terminating on the through-going x~698 column (#5 source above, #12 drain below). JUNCTION.
  S18 (383,590) - T, the y=590 rail's left half terminating on the through-going x~385 column (#6 source above, #13 drain below). JUNCTION.
  S38 (160,723), S39 (309,726), S40 (388,730), S41 (690,731), S42 (803,732) - all T's where a column drops onto the bottom rail; inkmap at S38 confirms a terminating stroke with a few px of pen overshoot, not a through-wire. JUNCTION for all five.
  Non-critical sites S4, S5, S7, S8, S22, S25-S30, S32-S34 are handwriting ('5V', '3V', '2KHz', '3KHz', '5A', '1A') brushing wire ink, or duplicate micro-sites inside a source symbol; none change a net.

PIN ORDER ON THE MOSFETS (this is the bulk of the corrections).
Every MOSFET on this sheet is drawn with the same template: an isolated gate bar with the gate lead leaving on its own side, a three-segment channel bar, and three stubs. The TOP stub runs to a lead that leaves on its own; the MIDDLE stub carries the body arrow and merges with the BOTTOM stub onto a single lead. Verified pixel-by-pixel with inkmap for #2 (x=386: continuous ink y=339..351 for the top lead, a clean white gap y=352..359, then continuous ink y=360..391 shared by the arrow stub and the bottom stub) and for #3 (x=222: ink y=332..347, gap y=348..353, ink y=354..384). So the body-arrow lead is the SOURCE and the isolated top lead is the DRAIN, uniformly. Arrow direction also confirms the annotated classes: it points toward the gate side on the N devices (#2, #6, #13) and away from it on the P devices (#3, #5, #12).
  #2 MOSFET-N (370,365): gate bar left. drain=p2 (T,386,331), gate=p0 (L,339,381), source=p1 (B,386,397). Tracer had t1 on the bottom lead and t2 on the gate - swapped. Fixed to t1->p0, t2->p1.
  #3 MOSFET-P (208,361): gate bar left. drain=p1 (T,222,330), gate=p2 (L,177,376), source=p0 (B,219,391). Fixed t1->p2, t2->p0.
  #5 MOSFET-P (723,470): MIRRORED - gate bar on the right at x~738, channel to its left, leads leaving leftwards. drain=p1 (T,710,438), gate=p2 (R,753,488), source=p0 (B,701,503). Fixed t1->p2, t2->p0.
  #6 MOSFET-N (374,518): gate bar left. drain=p1 (T,387,483), gate=p0 (L,340,537), source=p2 (B,387,551). Tracer already correct; left alone.
  #12 MOSFET-P (710,670): MIRRORED - gate bar on the right at x~727. drain=p0 (T,696,639), gate=p2 (R,741,687), source=p1 (B,690,699). Fixed t1->p2, t2->p1.
  #13 MOSFET-N (369,661): gate bar left. drain=p0 (T,382,628), gate=p2 (L,339,676), source=p1 (B,385,692). Fixed t1->p2, t2->p1.
Note the physical reading (drain toward the supply, source toward ground) agrees with the ink for the N devices; for the P devices (#3, #5, #12) the drawn body arrow puts the source on the lower lead, which is the reverse of how a designer would bias a PMOS. These are randomly generated schematics, so the ink is taken as authoritative and is stated here explicitly.

CLASSES: all 14 accepted as annotated. The MOSFET body-arrow directions independently confirm N vs P for all six transistors; the zener's bent cathode bar is clear; #0 is a circle with '+ -' inside (V-DC) and #9/#11 carry sine symbols (V-AC) while #8/#10 carry sine + arrow (I-AC).

  nB = {3.2 (source of MOSFET-P #3), 5.0 (drain of MOSFET-P #5)}  -- the y=438 rail
i.e. the N-chain (n1 -#2- nA -#6- n7 -#13- n8) and the P-chain

WHY (this is new evidence the first pass did not have; the pixel reading of S10
itself is not in dispute -- inkmap at (386,438) does show a plain 3px column
crossing a plain 2px rail with no dot and no jog, exactly as recorded above):

1. SIBLING INK, not sibling net count. Both human-verified siblings of this
   generated circuit contain the STRUCTURALLY IDENTICAL intersection -- the
   column joining the two series MOSFETs of one chain crossing the horizontal
   run joining the two series MOSFETs of the other chain -- and in both it is
   drawn as a bare X and read as a CROSSING:
   * circuit_437 at (616,405): crop at 12x is a perfectly plain X, no dot, no
     hop. Verified GT keeps n6={MOSFET-P 6 source, MOSFET-N 11 drain} and
     n7={MOSFET-N 5 source, MOSFET-P 9 drain} as two separate 2-terminal nets,
     which is only possible if that X is a crossing.
   * circuit_963 at (519,437): same bare X. Verified GT keeps
     n4={MOSFET-N 10 source, MOSFET-N 11 drain} (2 terminals) separate from
     n6={MOSFET-P 6 source, MOSFET-P 12 drain, Resistor 5} (3 terminals).
2. The "drafter jogs when he means not-connected" argument that decided the
   first pass is exactly the pattern the siblings show too -- and they still
   leave this one crossing bare. In circuit_963 the gate column hops the
   horizontal at (435,437) and hops the gate rail at (440,510) with textbook
   semicircles, yet crosses it bare at (519,437). In circuit_437 the gate
   column hops at (508,405) and the chain column crosses bare at (616,405).
   circuit_483 reproduces this one-for-one: the MOSFET-N #2 gate column jogs at
   S9 (296,438) and S13 (282,538), and the chain column crosses bare at S10.
   So on this drafter family's sheets a bare X is the mark used for a
   chain-to-chain crossing; the jog is reserved for gate wires.
3. The generic "bare X is usually a junction" prior is only about 2:1, not a
   rule. Measured over 60 verified cal sheets: critical deg-4 bare-X sites
   (hop<=6, dot<=2.4) resolve 53 junction / 27 crossing. A 2:1 prior does not
   survive two independent verified drawings of the SAME generated circuit both
   showing the crossing.
4. Topology check. With S10 as a junction MOSFET #2 and MOSFET #3 would sit in
   parallel between n1 and n3 -- a degeneracy neither sibling has. With S10 as
   a crossing the netlist is one terminal away from both siblings' structure
   (net-size multiset [2,2,2,2,2,2,3,3,4,4,7] vs their [2,2,2,2,2,3,3,3,4,4,6]).

RE-CONFIRMED, NOT CHANGED: that single remaining difference from the siblings is
MOSFET-N #13's gate. In both siblings the V-AC that feeds the top device's gate
also feeds the bottom device's gate of the same chain (437: n4 -> gates of #6
and #13; 963: n2 -> gates of #10 and #8). Here it does not: zoom at 7x on
(320,660) shows #13's gate lead leaving the gate bar at (350,713), running left
along y=713 to x=310, then straight down to a clean 3-branch T on the bottom
rail at S39 (309,726) -- no ink continues below the rail and nothing joins the
column between y=600 and y=713 (the n2 column stops at (287,600) and turns
left). So 13.1 (gate) and 13.2 (source) really are both on n8 and #13 really is
drawn as a dead device. That is the drawing, and it is left alone.
